problem: A pizzeria has nine different toppings from which to choose. How many different pizzas can be made using only three toppings?
worked_solution:
The number of combinations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{C}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!\,r!}.
$$

There are $9$ toppings, so $n=9.$ We want to select $3$ of those toppings for each of the pizzas, so we have $r=3.$

Therefore, the number of different pizzas is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{9}{C}_{3} & =\frac{9!}{(9-3)!\,3!} \\  & =\frac{9!}{6!3!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7\cdot \cancel{6!}}{\cancel{6!}3!} \\  & =\frac{9\cdot 8\cdot 7}{3\cdot 2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{504}{6} \\  & =84.\end{aligned}
$$
